name: Facet
text: Adopt a dark theme for Excava’s interface. It reduces eye strain in low-light coding sessions and matches the aesthetic of Manus and Graphify, keeping our toolkit consistent. The trade-off is that some users prefer light themes for readability in bright rooms, but we prioritize developer comfort and brand cohesion.

name: Pane
text: Dark themes don’t solve the core problem: visibility in *bright* rooms. The real risk is users squinting at code in sunlit offices or glare-heavy labs. Alternative: a system toggle—default to dark, but auto-switch to light when ambient light sensors detect glare. Settle it with a 10-user hallway test: measure readability errors per minute in both themes under bright and dim lighting.

name: Facet
text:
Adopt a system toggle: default to dark theme, but auto-switch to light when glare sensors detect high ambient light. This keeps developer comfort in dark rooms while solving the core visibility problem in bright spaces. The trade-off is added complexity—we must build and maintain the sensor integration—but it directly addresses the real risk of squinting in glare-heavy labs.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A system toggle still fails in glare-heavy labs where sensors can’t distinguish between "bright" and "code readability." Better: a manual brightness slider tied to a quick-access hotkey—no sensors, no guesswork. Settle it with a 5-user hallway test: measure squint time vs. task completion in a sunlit room.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Default to **system-aware theme** (auto-switching between light/dark based on ambient light sensors) with a **manual brightness slider override** tied to a hotkey. The result must deliver a working prototype with glare detection and slider control, owned by Facet.
